nodes.name: Authentication middleware
nodes.summary: Four factories that gate routes behind HTTP Basic Auth, Bearer tokens, JSON Web Tokens or remote JSON Web Key Sets.
nodes.detail: Each factory validates the incoming Authorization header (or a cookie fallback for JWT/JWK) and either calls next() on success or throws an HTTPException with a WWW-Authenticate header. basic-auth decodes the Base64 credential from the Authorization header and compares username/password pairs with timingSafeEqual to prevent timing attacks, with an optional verifyUser callback. bearer-auth extracts the token after the 'Bearer ' prefix and runs timingSafeEqual or a custom verifyToken function. jwt calls Jwt.verify (from utils/jwt) with an HMAC or RSA/EC key and stores the decoded payload at c.var.jwtPayload. jwk calls Jwt.verifyWithJwks, which accepts an inline keys array and/or a jwks_uri from which it fetches the JWKS document over HTTPS; both are merged before verification.

nodes.name: Security & headers middleware
nodes.summary: Four factories that protect against Cross-Origin Resource Sharing misuse, Cross-Site Request Forgery, clickjacking and other header-level attacks.
nodes.detail: cors sets Access-Control headers on every response and handles preflight OPTIONS requests returning 204, with configurable origin (string, list, or async function), allowed methods, allowed headers, max-age and credentials flag. csrf checks non-safe methods with form-like content types against the Sec-Fetch-Site header (default: same-origin) and the Origin header; if neither passes it throws HTTPException(403). secure-headers injects a fixed set of defensive response headers (Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, etc.), optionally builds a Content-Security-Policy with per-request nonce support via NONCE, and can remove X-Powered-By. powered-by is the inverse: it sets X-Powered-By to 'Hono' (or a custom value).

nodes.name: Response shaping middleware
nodes.summary: Middleware that transforms or augments the outgoing response: ETag, compression, body limiting, pretty JSON, trailing-slash redirects, request IDs and IP restriction.
nodes.detail: etag generates a SHA-1 (or custom) digest of the response body and sets the ETag header; it short-circuits to 304 when the client's If-None-Match matches. compress pipes the response body through a CompressionStream (gzip or deflate) when the content type is compressible, the threshold is met, and the client advertises the encoding via Accept-Encoding; it also weakens any strong ETag. bodyLimit reads the stream and rejects requests over maxSize bytes with 413. prettyJSON re-serialises the JSON body with configurable indentation when the ?pretty query param (or force option) is set. trimTrailingSlash and appendTrailingSlash issue 301 redirects on 404s (or immediately with alwaysRedirect). requestId reads X-Request-Id from the incoming request (generating a UUID if absent or malformed) and stores it in c.var.requestId. ipRestriction matches the client address against CIDR allow/deny rules built at startup.

nodes.name: Delivery & caching middleware
nodes.summary: Three factories that serve static files, cache responses with the Web Cache API, and render JSX layouts.
nodes.detail: serveStatic is a runtime-agnostic base that accepts a getContent callback supplied by each runtime adapter; it resolves the file path, negotiates pre-compressed variants (Brotli, Zstandard and gzip files), sets Content-Type via mime-type lookup, and delegates actual I/O to the callback. cache uses globalThis.caches (the Web Cache API) to store and replay GET and QUERY responses; it generates a cache key from the URL, optional Vary headers and an SHA-256 digest of the QUERY body, and respects Cache-Control directives. jsxRenderer sets a layout component and renderer function on the context so that c.render(<Node />) produces an HTML or streaming response with an optional DOCTYPE prepend; useRequestContext exposes the Hono Context inside any JSX component.

nodes.name: Control flow middleware
nodes.summary: Middleware that changes request routing: combine logic, method override, 405 detection, timeouts, timing, context storage, sub-app mounting and language detection.
nodes.detail: combine provides some/every/except combinators that compose other middleware with short-circuit or gate semantics. methodOverride reads the intended method from a form field, header or query param and re-dispatches to app.fetch with a new Request. methodNotAllowed lazily builds a TrieRouter from app.routes and returns 405 with an Allow header when the path matches but the method does not. timeout races next() against a setTimeout and throws HTTPException(504) on expiry. timing injects Server-Timing headers with per-label start/end timers and a total duration. contextStorage wraps each request in AsyncLocalStorage so getContext() works from anywhere in the call stack without passing Context explicitly. mount proxies a sub-request to a foreign application handler after rewriting the path prefix. languageDetector detects the preferred language from query param, cookie, Accept-Language header or URL path and stores it in c.var.language.

nodes.name: Logger middleware
nodes.summary: Single-module request/response logger that prints method, path, status and elapsed time.
nodes.detail: logger wraps next() and emits two lines: an incoming arrow before next() and an outgoing arrow with ANSI-colored status code and elapsed time after. The print function defaults to console.log but can be replaced for custom sinks.

nodes.name: Basic Auth middleware
nodes.summary: Exports basicAuth(): a factory for HTTP Basic Authentication middleware.
nodes.detail: Accepts a static username/password pair (or a list of pairs) or a verifyUser callback. At request time it decodes the Authorization header using utils/basic-auth, then compares each stored pair with timingSafeEqual (from utils/buffer) to prevent timing attacks. On failure it throws HTTPException(401) with a WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm=... header. An onAuthSuccess callback can inject user data into context variables after a successful match.

nodes.name: basicAuth()
nodes.summary: Returns a MiddlewareHandler that enforces HTTP Basic Authentication.

nodes.name: Bearer Auth middleware
nodes.summary: Exports bearerAuth(): a factory for static or callback-validated Bearer token authentication.
nodes.detail: Splits the Authorization header on whitespace, checks the prefix (default 'Bearer'), then either runs timingSafeEqual against one or more stored tokens or delegates to verifyToken. The three failure modes (no header, malformed header, wrong token) return 401/400 with customizable WWW-Authenticate and body values. A hashFunction option allows HMAC-based safe comparison.

nodes.name: bearerAuth()
nodes.summary: Returns a MiddlewareHandler that validates a Bearer token from Authorization header.

nodes.name: JWT Auth middleware implementation
nodes.summary: Exports jwt(): verifies a Bearer JWT and stores the decoded payload in c.var.jwtPayload.
nodes.detail: Reads the token from Authorization: Bearer <token> (or a named cookie fallback, optionally signed). Calls Jwt.verify (from utils/jwt) with the configured secret and algorithm; on failure throws HTTPException(401) with a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer header that quotes realm, error and error_description. The alg option is required; supported algorithms span HMAC (HS256/384/512), RSA-PKCS1 (RS256/384/512), RSA-PSS (PS256/384/512), ECDSA (ES256/384/512) and EdDSA. After successful verification ctx.set('jwtPayload', payload) makes the claims available as c.var.jwtPayload.

nodes.name: jwt()
nodes.summary: Factory that returns a MiddlewareHandler enforcing JWT Bearer authentication.
nodes.signature: jwt(options: { secret, alg, cookie?, headerName?, realm?, verification? }): MiddlewareHandler

nodes.name: JWT middleware entry
nodes.summary: Re-exports jwt, verify, decode, sign and AlgorithmTypes from jwt.ts; augments ContextVariableMap with jwtPayload.
nodes.detail: Public entry point for the JWT Auth middleware subpath. Re-exports the jwt factory and the lower-level Jwt.verify, Jwt.decode and Jwt.sign utilities so callers can build tokens without importing from utils directly. Augments the ContextVariableMap interface so c.var.jwtPayload is typed.

nodes.name: JWK Auth middleware implementation
nodes.summary: Exports jwk(): verifies a JWT using JSON Web Key Set keys fetched from a remote URI or supplied inline.
nodes.detail: Identical token-extraction logic to jwt middleware (Authorization header or cookie). Then calls Jwt.verifyWithJwks with the merged key set: inline keys from the keys option and/or keys fetched from the jwks_uri endpoint over HTTPS. The alg option restricts accepted asymmetric algorithms (RS, PS, ES, EdDSA families). Supports allow_anon to pass unauthenticated requests through. On success stores the payload in c.var.jwtPayload.

nodes.name: jwk()
nodes.summary: Factory that returns a MiddlewareHandler enforcing JWT authentication via a JWKS endpoint or inline keys.
nodes.signature: jwk(options: { keys?, jwks_uri?, allow_anon?, alg, verification? }, init?: RequestInit): MiddlewareHandler

nodes.name: JWK middleware entry
nodes.summary: Re-exports the jwk factory from jwk.ts.
nodes.detail: Thin barrel that surfaces the jwk factory for the hono/jwk subpath export. The implementation lives in jwk.ts; this file solely re-exports it.

nodes.name: CORS middleware
nodes.summary: Exports cors(): sets Cross-Origin Resource Sharing headers and handles preflight OPTIONS requests.
nodes.detail: Options: origin (string, string[], or async function; default '*'), allowMethods (array or async function; default GET/HEAD/PUT/POST/DELETE/PATCH/QUERY), allowHeaders (default []), exposeHeaders (default []), maxAge (seconds for Access-Control-Max-Age), credentials (boolean). For every request it resolves the allowed origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin. On OPTIONS it returns 204 with Access-Control-Allow-Methods and Access-Control-Allow-Headers (falling back to the request's Access-Control-Request-Headers). When origin is not '*', it appends Vary: Origin on every response.
facts: Default allowMethods: GET, HEAD, PUT, POST, DELETE, PATCH, QUERY
Vary: Origin appended when origin is not '*'

nodes.name: cors()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that manages CORS headers and handles preflight responses.

nodes.name: CSRF protection middleware
nodes.summary: Exports csrf(): blocks non-safe requests with form-like bodies when neither Sec-Fetch-Site nor Origin passes.
nodes.detail: Only intercepts methods that are not GET/HEAD/OPTIONS and have a content-type of application/x-www-form-urlencoded, multipart/form-data, or text/plain (the CSRF-susceptible types). It first checks the Sec-Fetch-Site header (default: must equal 'same-origin'). If that passes the request is allowed. Otherwise it checks the Origin header against the configured origin list. If both fail it throws HTTPException(403). The secFetchSite option accepts 'same-origin', 'same-site', 'cross-site', 'none', an array of those, or a custom function.
facts: Default origin: same as request URL origin
Only blocks application/x-www-form-urlencoded, multipart/form-data, text/plain bodies
Safe methods GET/HEAD/OPTIONS are always allowed through

nodes.name: csrf()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that blocks Cross-Site Request Forgery attempts.

nodes.name: Secure Headers middleware implementation
nodes.summary: Exports secureHeaders() and NONCE: injects defensive HTTP response headers.
nodes.detail: DEFAULT_OPTIONS enables: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy (same-origin), Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy (same-origin), Origin-Agent-Cluster (?1), Referrer-Policy (no-referrer), Strict-Transport-Security (max-age=15552000; includeSubDomains), X-Content-Type-Options (nosniff), X-DNS-Prefetch-Control (off), X-Download-Options (noopen), X-Frame-Options (SAMEORIGIN), X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies (none), X-XSS-Protection (0), removePoweredBy (true). Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy is off by default. The contentSecurityPolicy option builds a CSP header from a structured object; callbacks receive the Context so NONCE can generate a per-request base64 nonce, stored at c.var.secureHeadersNonce. The overwrite option (default true) controls whether to replace handler-set headers.
facts: NONCE generates a 16-byte random base64 nonce per request

nodes.name: secureHeaders()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that sets security-focused response headers.

nodes.name: NONCE
nodes.summary: CSP directive handler that generates or retrieves a per-request base64 nonce stored in c.var.secureHeadersNonce.

nodes.name: Secure Headers entry
nodes.summary: Re-exports NONCE and secureHeaders from secure-headers.ts; augments ContextVariableMap with secureHeadersNonce.
nodes.detail: Public barrel for the hono/secure-headers subpath. Re-exports NONCE and secureHeaders from secure-headers.ts and augments ContextVariableMap so c.var.secureHeadersNonce is typed as string | undefined.

nodes.name: Permissions Policy types
nodes.summary: Exports the PermissionsPolicyDirective union type listing all known Permissions-Policy feature names.
nodes.detail: Contains the exhaustive PermissionsPolicyDirective string union covering all W3C Permissions Policy feature names (camera, geolocation, fullscreen, etc.). Imported by secure-headers.ts to give the permissionsPolicy option strong typing.

nodes.name: Powered By middleware
nodes.summary: Exports poweredBy(): sets X-Powered-By to 'Hono' (or a custom serverName) on every response.
nodes.detail: Single-function module. poweredBy() runs after next() and sets the X-Powered-By response header. The default value is 'Hono'. Used in the reverse direction from secureHeaders which removes the header.

nodes.name: poweredBy()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that appends X-Powered-By to responses.

nodes.name: ETag middleware
nodes.summary: Exports etag(): computes a digest of the response body, sets ETag, and returns 304 when it matches If-None-Match.
nodes.detail: After next() it checks whether the response is a successful GET/HEAD/QUERY. If the response has no existing ETag it generates one by streaming the body through generateDigest (SHA-1 by default). If the client's If-None-Match header matches, it cancels the body stream and returns a minimal 304 Not Modified response retaining only cache-safe headers (Cache-Control, Content-Location, Date, ETag, Expires, Vary). The weak option prepends W/ to produce weak ETags.
facts: Default digest algorithm: SHA-1 via crypto.subtle
RETAINED_304_HEADERS: cache-control, content-location, date, etag, expires, vary

nodes.name: etag()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that manages ETag caching for GET/HEAD/QUERY responses.

nodes.name: ETag digest helper
nodes.summary: Streams a ReadableStream through a custom hash function in 256 KB chunks and returns a hex digest string.
nodes.detail: generateDigest reads a ReadableStream in 256 KB chunks, calls the generator callback for each chunk, and returns the final digest as a lowercase hex string. Handles streaming body consumption without loading the entire body into memory at once.

nodes.name: Compress middleware
nodes.summary: Exports compress(): pipes compressible response bodies through gzip or deflate CompressionStream.
nodes.detail: After next(), checks Content-Type against COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX (from utils/compress), Content-Length against the threshold (default 1024 bytes), absence of Content-Encoding and Transfer-Encoding, and Cache-Control: no-transform. Negotiates the encoding from Accept-Encoding using parseAccept (from utils/accept); gzip is preferred. Sets Content-Encoding, removes Content-Length, and downgrades any strong ETag to a weak one. Also sets Vary: Accept-Encoding.
facts: Converts strong ETag to weak after compression

nodes.name: compress()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that compresses responses using the CompressionStream Web API.

nodes.name: Body Limit middleware
nodes.summary: Exports bodyLimit(): enforces a maximum request body size, returning 413 on overflow.
nodes.detail: When only Content-Length is present (no Transfer-Encoding), it checks the header value directly. When Transfer-Encoding is present, it reads the body stream chunk by chunk into a growing Uint8Array and aborts if the accumulated size exceeds maxSize. After reading, it replaces c.req.raw with a new Request whose body is the buffered bytes, so downstream handlers can still parse it normally.
facts: Default error response: 413 Payload Too Large
Respects Transfer-Encoding over Content-Length per RFC 7230
Buffers the full body before calling next()

nodes.name: bodyLimit()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that rejects request bodies larger than maxSize bytes.

nodes.name: Pretty JSON middleware
nodes.summary: Exports prettyJSON(): reformats JSON response bodies with configurable indentation.
nodes.detail: After next(), checks the response Content-Type against a JSON regex. When the query param (default 'pretty') is present or force:true, it clones the response, parses the JSON, and re-serialises with JSON.stringify at the configured space count (default 2). Removes the stale Content-Length header after reformatting.
facts: Activated by ?pretty or ?pretty='' in the URL, or force:true option

nodes.name: prettyJSON()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that pretty-prints JSON responses on request.

nodes.name: Trailing Slash middleware
nodes.summary: Exports trimTrailingSlash() and appendTrailingSlash(): issue 301 redirects to normalize URL trailing slashes.
nodes.detail: trimTrailingSlash removes a trailing slash from GET/HEAD paths. appendTrailingSlash adds one if absent. Both have an alwaysRedirect option; without it they only redirect when the response is 404 (lazy redirect). appendTrailingSlash also accepts a skip function to exclude paths with file extensions.
facts: alwaysRedirect:true redirects before next(); default redirects only on 404

nodes.name: trimTrailingSlash()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that removes trailing slashes via 301 redirect.

nodes.name: appendTrailingSlash()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that appends a trailing slash via 301 redirect.

nodes.name: Request ID middleware implementation
nodes.summary: Exports requestId(): reads or generates a request identifier and stores it in c.var.requestId.
nodes.detail: Reads the X-Request-Id header (configurable via headerName). If absent, too long (>255 chars), or containing characters outside [\w\-=], it generates a new UUID via crypto.randomUUID(). The id is stored with c.set('requestId') and echoed back in the response header. The generator option replaces the UUID factory.

nodes.name: requestId()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that assigns a unique identifier to each request.

nodes.name: Request ID entry
nodes.summary: Re-exports requestId and RequestIdVariables; augments ContextVariableMap with requestId.
nodes.detail: Public barrel for hono/request-id. Re-exports the requestId factory and RequestIdVariables type from request-id.ts, and augments ContextVariableMap so c.var.requestId is typed as string.

nodes.name: IP Restriction middleware
nodes.summary: Exports ipRestriction(): blocks or allows requests based on client IP address with static, CIDR and function rules.
nodes.detail: buildMatcher compiles the denyList/allowList into fast bitwise CIDR matchers (using BigInt arithmetic) and static string sets. At request time the client IP is obtained from a getConnInfo adapter function. The deny check runs first; if matched it returns 403. The allow check runs next; if matched it passes. If neither list applies (empty allowList) the request passes. IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (::ffff:x.x.x.x) are normalised so IPv4 rules match both forms.
facts: Rules accept: static IP, CIDR notation, or function (addr, type) => boolean
IPv4-mapped IPv6 (::ffff:x.x.x.x) matched by IPv4 rules

nodes.name: ipRestriction()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that enforces IP allow/deny rules.

nodes.name: Serve Static base middleware
nodes.summary: Exports the runtime-agnostic serveStatic() base; actual file I/O is delegated to a getContent callback supplied by each runtime adapter.
nodes.detail: Resolves the requested path relative to root using the join function (defaultJoin or a runtime-provided one). Performs path traversal safety checks (rejects ../ and double slashes). If isDir returns true, appends index.html. When precompressed:true, checks for Brotli, Zstandard and gzip variants in Accept-Encoding order and serves the best match. Sets Content-Type from getMimeType (utils/mime). Calls onFound on success and onNotFound on miss (then falls through to next()). Skips non-GET/HEAD requests and already-finalized responses.
facts: Pre-compressed encodings checked in order: br, zstd, gzip
Path traversal blocked via regex on ../ and double slashes

nodes.name: serveStatic()
nodes.summary: Runtime-agnostic static file serving factory; file reading is provided by the runtime adapter via getContent.
nodes.signature: serveStatic<E>(options: ServeStaticOptions & { getContent, join?, isDir? }): MiddlewareHandler

nodes.name: Serve Static path helper
nodes.summary: Exports defaultJoin(): joins URL path segments with '/' normalising multiple slashes and resolving . and .. segments.
nodes.detail: defaultJoin concatenates non-empty path segments with '/', normalises consecutive slashes, then resolves . and .. segments in a single pass. Does not support Windows backslash paths; for Windows support callers should pass Node's path.join as the join option to serveStatic.

nodes.name: Cache middleware
nodes.summary: Exports cache(): stores and replays GET/QUERY responses using the Web Cache API (globalThis.caches).
nodes.detail: Cache key is built as a synthetic URL under /.hono/cache, appending cacheName, method, an SHA-256 digest of the QUERY body (from utils/crypto), and Vary header values. For GET requests the key is deterministic. For QUERY requests a body digest is computed; if body is too large (default 64 KB) or FormData, the request bypasses the cache. After next(), responses are skipped if the status is not in cacheableStatusCodes (default [200]), if Cache-Control is private/no-store/no-cache, or if Set-Cookie is present. The wait option (default false) controls whether cache.put is awaited or handed to executionCtx.waitUntil().
facts: wait:false uses executionCtx.waitUntil() for non-blocking cache writes
Vary '*' in options throws an Error

nodes.name: cache()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that serves and stores responses via the Web Cache API.
nodes.signature: cache(options: { cacheName, wait?, cacheControl?, vary?, keyGenerator?, maxQueryBodySize?, cacheableStatusCodes? }): MiddlewareHandler

nodes.name: JSX Renderer middleware
nodes.summary: Exports jsxRenderer() and useRequestContext(): sets a layout component on the context and wires c.render() to produce HTML or streamed responses.
nodes.detail: jsxRenderer installs a renderer closure on the context via c.setRenderer(). The closure wraps the page content in the layout component (or Fragment), prepends a DOCTYPE, and either calls c.html() for a standard response or c.body(renderToReadableStream(...)) for a streaming response. RequestContext is a JSX context that exposes the Hono Context inside any server-rendered component; useRequestContext() retrieves it.

nodes.name: jsxRenderer()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that installs a JSX layout and renderer on the request context.

nodes.name: useRequestContext()
nodes.summary: Hook that returns the current Hono Context from inside a JSX server component.
nodes.signature: useRequestContext<E, P, I>(): Context<E, P, I>

nodes.name: Combine middleware
nodes.summary: Exports some(), every() and except(): combinators that compose multiple middleware with OR, AND and NOT-IF semantics.
nodes.detail: some() runs each handler in order and stops at the first success; if all throw or return false the last error is re-thrown. every() uses compose() (from hono-core) to run all handlers in sequence; if any returns false it throws 'Unmet condition'. except() builds a TrieRouter from path patterns and uses some(matchCondition, every(...middleware)) so paths matching the condition bypass the middleware.

nodes.name: some()
nodes.summary: Returns a MiddlewareHandler that runs the first middleware to succeed and stops.

nodes.name: every()
nodes.summary: Returns a MiddlewareHandler that runs all given middleware; throws if any returns false or throws.

nodes.name: except()
nodes.summary: Returns a MiddlewareHandler that skips the given middleware when the condition or path pattern matches.

nodes.name: Method Override middleware
nodes.summary: Exports methodOverride(): reads an intended HTTP method from a form field, header, or query param and re-dispatches to app.fetch.
nodes.detail: Supports three source modes: form field (default _method in multipart or urlencoded body), custom header, or query parameter. Constructs a new Request with the overridden method, stripping body-related headers for body-less methods (GET/HEAD). Passes the modified request to options.app.fetch along with the env and executionCtx from the original context, so the full Hono routing chain runs again.
facts: Re-dispatches to app.fetch, not just calls next()
Skips override logic entirely for GET requests

nodes.name: methodOverride()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that enables HTTP method tunnelling via form field, header or query param.

nodes.name: Method Not Allowed middleware
nodes.summary: Exports methodNotAllowed(): detects when a 404 response is due to a wrong HTTP method and upgrades it to a 405 with an Allow header.
nodes.detail: On first use it lazily builds a TrieRouter from app.routes, mapping each registered path to the set of allowed methods (HEAD is added automatically for GET routes). After next(), if the response is 404 and there is no error, it looks up the request path in the TrieRouter. If allowed methods exist but the current method is not among them, it replaces the response with a 405 that sets Allow: GET, POST, ... A custom onMethodNotAllowed callback can generate the response instead.

nodes.name: methodNotAllowed()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that upgrades 404 responses to 405 when the path is known but the method is not.

nodes.name: Timeout middleware
nodes.summary: Exports timeout(): races the downstream chain against a setTimeout and throws HTTPException(504) on expiry.
nodes.detail: Creates a Promise that rejects after duration milliseconds with the given exception (default HTTPException 504 Gateway Timeout). Calls Promise.race([next(), timeoutPromise]); the timer is always cleared in the finally block to prevent leaks. The exception parameter accepts an HTTPException instance or a function that receives the context and returns one.
facts: Timer cleared in finally block regardless of outcome

nodes.name: timeout()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that aborts slow handlers after a given number of milliseconds.
nodes.signature: timeout(duration: number, exception?: HTTPExceptionFunction | HTTPException): MiddlewareHandler

nodes.name: Server-Timing middleware implementation
nodes.summary: Exports timing(), setMetric(), startTime(), endTime(), wrapTime(): Server-Timing header instrumentation.
nodes.detail: timing() stores a metric bucket in c.var.metric (headers array + timers Map). It starts a 'total' timer around next(). After next() it ends all auto-end timers and joins them into a Server-Timing response header. crossOrigin adds Timing-Allow-Origin. setMetric() pushes a named metric with an optional duration and description. startTime/endTime bracket arbitrary async operations; wrapTime wraps a Promise. All helpers warn if the timing() middleware is not installed.
facts: total timer default: enabled, description 'Total Response Time'
autoEnd default: true (ends all open timers after next())

nodes.name: timing()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that appends Server-Timing headers tracking request duration.

nodes.name: startTime()
nodes.summary: Records the start time of a named timer in the request's metric bucket.
nodes.signature: startTime(c: Context, name: string, description?: string): void

nodes.name: endTime()
nodes.summary: Ends a named timer, computes elapsed milliseconds and adds a Server-Timing entry.
nodes.signature: endTime(c: Context, name: string, precision?: number): void

nodes.name: Context Storage middleware
nodes.summary: Exports contextStorage(), getContext(), tryGetContext(): makes the Hono Context available via AsyncLocalStorage.
nodes.detail: contextStorage() wraps each request in asyncLocalStorage.run(c, next) so any synchronous or asynchronous code called during the request can retrieve the context via getContext() without prop-drilling. getContext() throws if called outside a request. tryGetContext() returns undefined instead. Relies on Node.js AsyncLocalStorage from node:async_hooks.

nodes.name: contextStorage()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that stores the Context in AsyncLocalStorage for the request lifetime.

nodes.name: getContext()
nodes.summary: Retrieves the current Hono Context from AsyncLocalStorage; throws if none is active.

nodes.name: Mount middleware
nodes.summary: Exports mount(): proxies requests to an external application handler after rewriting the path prefix.
nodes.detail: defaultReplaceRequest creates a new Request with the mount base path stripped from the URL using createMountedRequest (from utils/mount) and routePath (from helper/route). The result is passed to applicationHandler along with c.env and c.executionCtx. If the external handler returns null/undefined, next() is called allowing Hono to continue. replaceRequest:false passes the original Request unchanged.

nodes.name: mount()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that delegates to an external application handler with path prefix rewriting.

nodes.name: Language Detector middleware implementation
nodes.summary: Exports languageDetector() and per-source detect functions; stores the matched language in c.var.language.
nodes.detail: Detection order (default: querystring, cookie, header) is configurable. detectFromQuery reads the 'lang' query param. detectFromCookie reads the 'language' cookie. detectFromHeader parses Accept-Language with q-values using parseAccept (from utils/accept) and walks entries discarding q=0. detectFromPath extracts a path segment by index. Each detector calls normalizeLanguage which does exact match, then RFC 4647 lookup truncation against supportedLanguages. The result is cached in a cookie by default.

nodes.name: languageDetector()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that detects the request language and sets c.var.language.

nodes.name: Language Detector entry
nodes.summary: Re-exports languageDetector and all detect* helpers; augments ContextVariableMap with language.
nodes.detail: Public barrel for hono/language. Re-exports languageDetector and the four strategy helpers (detectFromCookie, detectFromHeader, detectFromPath, detectFromQuery) from language.ts, and augments ContextVariableMap so c.var.language is typed as string.

nodes.name: Logger middleware
nodes.summary: Exports logger(): prints method, path, status (ANSI-colored) and elapsed time to a print function.
nodes.detail: Logs two lines per request: '<-- METHOD /path' before next() and '--> METHOD /path STATUS elapsed' after. Status codes are colored by HTTP class (2xx green, 3xx cyan, 4xx yellow, 5xx red) using utils/color. The elapsed time is humanized to ms or s. The print function defaults to console.log.

nodes.name: logger()
nodes.summary: Factory returning a MiddlewareHandler that logs each request with timing and color-coded status.

nodes.name: Server-Timing entry
nodes.summary: Re-exports timing, setMetric, startTime, endTime, wrapTime and TimingVariables; augments ContextVariableMap with metric.

flows.name: Request through cors() then jwt() to route handler
flows.summary: Shows how CORS headers are set before JWT verification runs; both middleware call next() on success.

steps.text: cors middleware runs first. It checks the Origin header and sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin. For a preflight OPTIONS request it returns 204 immediately without calling next(). For normal requests it sets the header and calls next(), passing control to the next middleware in the chain.

jwt middleware runs next. It reads the Authorization: Bearer <token> header (or a cookie fallback if configured). It calls Jwt.verify with the secret and algorithm. If verification fails it throws HTTPException(401) with a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer header and the chain stops. On success it stores the decoded payload in c.var.jwtPayload and calls next().

The route handler now executes. It can read c.var.jwtPayload for the authenticated user's claims. When the handler returns, the CORS Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is already on the response from step 1 because cors set it on c.res.headers before calling next().

flows.name: JWT middleware rejecting a missing or invalid Bearer token
flows.summary: Shows the exact path jwt() takes when the Authorization header is absent or the token signature fails.

steps.text: jwt middleware reads the Authorization header. If it is absent (and no cookie option is configured) it immediately constructs a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="...",error="invalid_request",error_description="no authorization included in request" header and throws HTTPException(401). The chain is unwound without calling next().

If a token is present but structurally malformed (not 'Bearer <value>') jwt throws 401 with error='invalid_request'. If the structure is correct it calls Jwt.verify with the configured secret and algorithm. Any verification error (bad signature, expired, wrong alg) leaves payload undefined.

With payload undefined, jwt throws HTTPException(401, { message: 'Unauthorized', res: ..., cause }) carrying the WWW-Authenticate header with error='invalid_token'. The Hono error handler catches it and returns the attached Response directly to the client.
